messages:
maya: Quick readout — ran a small priming + int8 sweep on nova-lite (7B-ish) across 1k eval slices. Trying to get rapid GTN/product guidance. TL;DR: decent cost savings, small hit on long-form recall. Details below. https://internal.redwood/bench/3555

kevin: Nice — can you paste the scorecard numbers?

maya: Scorecard (1k sample, mixed convo/longform):
```
metric            | fp16 (base) | int8 | delta
EM (exact match)  | 0.872       | 0.864 | -0.9%
ROUGE-L           | 0.412       | 0.405 | -1.7%
Latency p50 (ms)  | 110         | 122   | +12ms
Cost / 1k tokens  | $0.42       | $0.29 | -31%
```
Notes: priming (2-4 prompt tokens of system-level context) improved int8 stability on short Q/A slices. Longform (>1k tokens) saw a larger quality drop (~2.5% EM) and slightly worse hallucination rate on a specific subset (product spec extraction).

anita: Which slices triggered hallucination more? any common patterns?

maya: Patterns: multi-step extraction and heavy numeric reasoning. Short clarifications and summarization were fine. Example problematic prompt: "Extract all bullet points and the numeric thresholds from the spec and normalize units." Int8 sometimes dropped a bullet.

sam: For routing: what's your recommendation for GTN defaults vs product features?

maya: Recommendation:
- Product-facing, long responses or critical-extract pipelines -> keep fp16 / higher-fidelity model (or fallback to fp16 if int8 hit is detected).
- GTN / self-serve interactive endpoints (short QAs, chatlets <512 tokens) -> default to int8 to save cost.
- Hybrid rule: if request.token_length > 1024 OR pattern == "extract/numeric", route to fp16. Otherwise int8.

Here's a minimal routing policy snippet to drop into the router config: 
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name": "high-fidelity", "predicate": "tokens>1024 || pattern==\"extract\"", "model": "nova-lite-fp16"},
    {"name": "cheap-interactive", "predicate": "default", "model": "nova-lite-int8"}
  ]
}
```

kevin: Nice. Any guardrails to detect regressions live?

maya: Yes — suggested guardrails:
- Shadow 1% of int8 traffic to fp16 and compute a rolling delta for key metrics (EM/ROUGE). Alert if delta > 1.5% over 30m.
- Run a tiny adversarial slice (100 examples) hourly.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for common conversational prefixes to reduce tokens and mitigate latency impact.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job created: canary/3555-int8 -> 1000 requests over 1h. Results will post to #eng-ml/bench-reports.

sam: For GTN handoff language: "Recommend enabling int8 by default for exploratory/self-serve, with opt-in high-fidelity route for long or extraction-heavy workloads. Monitor shadow deltas and set auto-fallback to fp16 if quality regresses."

anita: Can you add a quick table for product showing cost savings vs expected impact? product wants a one-slide snippet.

maya: Sure — quick one-line: "Estimate: ~30% token cost reduction, expected end-user accuracy drop 0.5-2.5% depending on workload; recommend hybrid routing and 1% shadowing for safety." I'll drop a short doc in GTN folder after the canary completes.

kevin: Thanks — appreciate the rapid triage. :thumbsup:

maya: Happy to iterate once canary results are back.
